title: Find the Maximum Length of a Good Subsequence I
summary: Given an integer array nums and a non-negative integer k, determine the longest subsequence where at most k indices have consecutive elements differing.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a non-negative integer k, determine the longest subsequence where at most k indices have consecutive elements differing. Return the length of this subsequence.
constraints: nums is nonempty and k is nonnegative.
Choose a subsequence in original index order; count adjacent chosen pairs whose values differ.
Return the maximum subsequence length whose differing-adjacency count is at most k.
hints: A subsequence ending at index i is determined for extension by its last value and number of changes used.
Use DP over ending index and change budget, extending every earlier endpoint.
dp[i][c]=max(dp[j][c-different]+1); initialize singleton states to one.
Every subsequence has a penultimate chosen index j, so the recurrence enumerates all and records the best length for each exact-or-at-most budget.
